tts: This program saves a temperature log as a CSV file, then reads it back and finds the highest reading.
import csv loads Python's module for CSV files.
open with w creates the file temps dot csv in write mode. with will close it automatically.
write puts four lines into the file: the header, time comma temp, and three readings. Each backslash n ends a line.
temps starts as an empty list, ready to collect the readings as numbers.
Now the file is opened again, this time for reading.
DictReader reads the header first. Then each row becomes a dictionary. The first row has time zero eight hundred, and temp thirty seven point two, still as text.
float turns the text into a number, and append adds it to temps.
The loop does the same for the other two rows.
print shows all three readings, now as numbers.
max finds the highest: thirty eight point four, at noon.

float turns the text into a number, and append adds it to the list.
The same happens for every line. Now max can find the highest reading.
